facts.statement: The genus Propristis was first described by Dames in 1883.
The type species of the genus is Propristis schweinfurthi.
A second valid species, Propristis mayumbensis, was described by Dartevelle and Casier in 1943.
Propristis is an extinct genus of sawfish.
facts.quote: Propristis is an extinct genus of sawfish

facts.statement: Fossils of Propristis have been found in Egypt, Cabinda, Morocco, Qatar, Spain, the United Kingdom, and the United States.
facts.quote: It has been found in Egypt, Cabinda, Morocco, Qatar, Spain, the United Kingdom, and the United States

facts.statement: The most common fossil remains of Propristis are isolated rostral denticles, though complete rostra have also been discovered.
facts.quote: Isolated rostral denticles are the most common remains, but rostra has also been found

facts.statement: Propristis belongs to the family Pristidae.
Propristis is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
Propristis lived from the Ypresian to the Chattian stages, between 56 and 23.04 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Ypresian to Chattian (56 to 23.04 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Propristis lived during the Eocene and Miocene epochs.
rejected.quote: It lived from the Eocene to the Miocene
